easy.def: A word used to compare two things.
examples: I am taller than you.
A cat is smaller than a dog.
She runs faster than me.

more.def: A word used to compare two things, showing how they are different.
examples: A blue whale is much bigger than an elephant.
I would rather read a book than watch television.
It took us more than an hour to get there.

easy.def: To say you are glad for what someone did.
examples: I thank my friend.
She thanked her aunt.
Let us thank the cook.

more.def: To tell someone that you are grateful for what they have given or done.
examples: We thanked the bus driver for the ride.
I wrote a card to thank my grandmother for the sweater.
The team thanked the fans for cheering.

easy.def: Glad and grateful.
examples: I am thankful for my family.
She was thankful.
We are thankful.

more.def: Feeling grateful and glad about something.
examples: I am thankful for my family and friends.
She was thankful for the help.
We are thankful that the storm passed.

easy.def: Luckily, with gratitude.
examples: Thankfully, no one was hurt.
She smiled thankfully.
Thankfully, it stopped raining.

more.def: In a way that shows thanks, or luckily.
examples: Thankfully, the lost kitten was found.
She smiled thankfully at the helper.
Thankfully, the rain stopped before the game.

easy.def: A word you say when someone is kind to you.
examples: Thanks for the gift!
Thanks, Mom.
Thanks for helping.

more.def: A short way to say that you are grateful for something.
examples: Thanks for holding the door for me.
Thanks, I would love a glass of water.
Thanks for the ride to school.

easy.def: Words that show you are glad.
examples: Give thanks to the cook.
She said thanks.
We gave our thanks.

more.def: Words or actions that show you are grateful.
examples: The class sent their thanks to the firefighters who visited.
He gave thanks for the meal before eating.
Many thanks for your help with the project.

easy.def: A holiday in November when families eat a big meal together.
examples: We eat turkey on Thanksgiving.
Thanksgiving is in November.
Family comes for Thanksgiving.

more.def: A holiday in the United States on the fourth Thursday of November, when people give thanks and share a big meal.
examples: Our family eats turkey and pie on Thanksgiving.
We say what we are thankful for at Thanksgiving dinner.
Thanksgiving is celebrated on the fourth Thursday in November.

easy.def: A word for something over there, away from you.
examples: What is that over there?
I like that.
That is my bike.

more.def: A word used to point to a person or thing farther away, or one just mentioned.
examples: Look at that tall building across the street.
That was the best movie I have seen all year.
Did you hear that strange noise outside?

easy.def: A word which links what someone says or thinks to the rest.
examples: I know that you are kind.
She said that lunch is ready.
I hope that it snows.

more.def: A word used to link what someone says or believes to words like say, think, know, or hope.
examples: Scientists believe that the dinosaurs lived millions of years ago.
My brother told me that the game was canceled.
We are glad that you could join our team.

easy.def: A roof made of straw or reeds.
examples: The house has a thatch roof.
The thatch is dry.
A thatch covers the house.

more.def: Straw, reeds or leaves used to make a roof.
examples: The cottage had a thatch roof.
The thatch kept the house cool in summer.
Workers laid fresh thatch on the old house.

easy.def: To melt or get warm after being frozen.
examples: The ice will thaw.
Mom let the meat thaw.
Snow thaws in spring.

more.def: To become soft or liquid after having been frozen, or to make something do this.
examples: The snow began to thaw as the spring sun grew warm.
Mom left the frozen peas on the counter to thaw.
The pond thawed in April.

easy.def: A warm spell when ice melts.
examples: The thaw came in March.
A thaw melted the snow.
We waited for the thaw.

more.def: A period of warmer weather when snow and ice melt.
examples: The first thaw of the spring turned the snow to slush.
A sudden thaw in January melted the ice on the road.
We waited eagerly for the thaw to start planting.

easy.def: A word used before a name for one special thing.
examples: Please close the door.
The dog is asleep.
I ate the apple.

more.def: A word used before a noun to show you mean one particular person or thing that is already known.
examples: The moon was bright last night.
Can you pass me the red marker?
The museum we visited is downtown.

easy.def: A place where you watch movies or plays.
examples: We saw a movie at the theater.
The theater is dark.
Let's go to the theater.

more.def: A building where people go to watch plays, movies or shows.
examples: We watched a movie at the theater.
The school theater has a big stage.
A play is on at the theater tonight.

easy.def: Having to do with plays and acting.
examples: She loves theatrical shows.
It was a theatrical event.
He is very theatrical.

more.def: Having to do with the theater, or acting in a dramatic way, as if on a stage.
examples: The school held a theatrical show with songs and costumes.
He gave a theatrical sigh and fell onto the couch.
She has a theatrical voice and loves to act.

easy.def: In a big, showy way, like an actor.
examples: She sighed theatrically.
He bowed theatrically.
She theatrically waved.

more.def: In an exaggerated way, as if acting on a stage.
examples: She sighed theatrically and put her hand on her forehead.
He bowed theatrically to the audience.
The boy theatrically fell onto the sofa.

easy.def: Acting in a big, dramatic way.
examples: His theatrics were funny.
She used theatrics.
The theatrics made us laugh.

more.def: Over-dramatic behavior, as if you were acting on a stage.
examples: His theatrics made the class laugh.
She used theatrics to get her way.
The magician's theatrics delighted the crowd.

easy.def: A very old word for "you."
examples: I thank thee.
"Come with me," said the king to thee.
Old books say thee.

more.def: An old-fashioned word for "you" that is used as the object of a sentence in very old books and poems.
examples: "I give thee my thanks," said the knight.
In an old poem, the poet wrote, "I love thee."
The old prayer says, "Bless thee and keep thee."

easy.def: Stealing.
examples: The theft was reported.
The theft of the bike was sad.
The police solved the theft.

more.def: The crime of stealing something.
examples: The theft of the bike was reported to the police.
The shop has an alarm to stop theft.
The museum added cameras after the theft.

easy.def: A word that shows something belongs to them.
examples: The kids lost their ball.
Their dog is big.
The birds fed their babies.

more.def: A word used to show that something belongs to or is connected with two or more people or things.
examples: The students put their backpacks on the hooks.
The bears protect their cubs from danger.
Their house is at the end of the road.

easy.def: A word for more than one person or thing.
examples: I saw them play.
Give them the books.
We like them.

more.def: A word used for two or more people, animals, or things when they are not the ones doing the action.
examples: The coach thanked them for their hard work.
I found my gloves, and I put them in my bag.
We watched the geese until we could not see them anymore.

easy.def: The main idea of something.
examples: The theme of the party is space.
The theme of the book is friendship.
The class chose a theme.

more.def: The main idea or subject of a story, party or other event.
examples: The theme of the party was pirates.
The theme of the story is friendship.
The class picked a theme for the art show.

easy.def: They, and not someone else.
examples: They made lunch themselves.
The kids dressed themselves.
They hurt themselves.

more.def: Used when "they" are the ones who do something and also receive it.
examples: The twins built the fort themselves.
The children dressed themselves.
The birds cleaned themselves in the puddle.

easy.def: After that.
examples: I ate, and then I played.
First wash, then dry.
Then she went home.

more.def: At that time, or next, after something else.
examples: Mix the flour and water, and then add the eggs.
We saw the lightning, and then we heard the thunder.
I was in kindergarten then, and I was very small.

easy.def: An idea that explains something.
examples: I have a theory.
Her theory was funny.
A theory about dinosaurs.

more.def: An idea that tries to explain something.
examples: I have a theory about why the cat sleeps there.
Scientists have a theory about how the moon formed.
His theory was that the dog hid the sock.

easy.def: A person who helps people feel or get better.
examples: The therapist helped him walk.
A therapist works with kids.
The therapist was kind.

more.def: A person who is trained to help people get better from an illness or injury.
examples: A therapist helped him walk again after his injury.
The speech therapist taught her to say the sound.
A therapist listened to her talk about her worries.

easy.def: Treatment that helps you feel better.
examples: She has therapy.
Therapy helps.
Physical therapy.

more.def: Treatment that helps a person get better from an illness or an injury, or helps them with their feelings.
examples: After he broke his arm, he went to therapy to make it strong again.
Talking to a counselor is a kind of therapy.
Swimming was good therapy for her sore back.

easy.def: In that place.
examples: Put the book there.
I will go there.
The cat is over there.

more.def: In or to a place that is not where you are, or at that place just mentioned.
examples: We drove to the beach and played there all afternoon.
Look over there, behind the big oak tree.
The store is closed, so there is no point going.

easy.def: For that reason.
examples: It was raining, so we therefore stayed inside.
I was tired, therefore I went to bed.
He studied; therefore he passed.

more.def: For that reason, as a result of what was just said.
examples: The road was icy, and therefore the bus drove slowly.
She studied hard and therefore did well on the test.
It was cold; therefore we wore our coats.

easy.def: Having to do with heat.
examples: I wore thermal socks in the snow.
The thermal cup kept my drink hot.
She put on a thermal shirt.

more.def: Having to do with heat, or made to keep heat in.
examples: Thermal underwear keeps skiers warm on cold mountains.
A thermal blanket kept the lost hiker from getting too cold.
Hot springs are heated by thermal energy from deep underground.

easy.def: A tool that tells how hot or cold something is.
examples: The thermometer says fifty.
I used a thermometer.
The nurse used a thermometer.

more.def: A tool that measures how hot or cold something is, such as the air, the weather or your body.
examples: The thermometer outside showed that it was ten degrees below zero.
The nurse put a thermometer under my tongue to check for a fever.
Mom used a thermometer to check the temperature of the soup.

easy.def: A bottle that keeps drinks hot or cold.
examples: I have a thermos of soup.
The thermos is full.
Dad packed a thermos.

more.def: A bottle with double walls that keeps hot drinks hot and cold drinks cold.
examples: Dad filled the thermos with hot cocoa.
She packed soup in a thermos for lunch.
The thermos kept the milk cold all day.

easy.def: A box on the wall that controls how hot a room is.
examples: Dad set the thermostat.
The thermostat is on the wall.
Turn up the thermostat.

more.def: A device that controls the heat in a room or building.
examples: Dad turned up the thermostat because it was cold.
The thermostat keeps the house at a steady warmth.
She set the thermostat to seventy degrees.

easy.def: A book of words with similar meanings.
examples: I used a thesaurus.
A thesaurus lists words.
The thesaurus helps me.

more.def: A book that lists words and gives other words with similar meanings.
examples: I looked in a thesaurus for another word for "big."
A thesaurus helps you find the right word.
The writer kept a thesaurus on her desk.

easy.def: A word for things that are close to you.
examples: These are my shoes.
I like these.
Look at these!

more.def: A word used for more than one person or thing that is near you or has just been mentioned.
examples: These berries are ripe, so we can pick them.
Put these papers in your backpack.
These are the animals we saw at the farm.

easy.def: A word for two or more people or things.
examples: They are my friends.
They play in the yard.
The birds are loud, and they sing.

more.def: A word used for two or more people, animals, or things that have already been talked about.
examples: The twins love swimming, and they practice every Saturday.
I cannot find my gloves, but I think they are in the car.
The farmers were happy because they had a good harvest.

easy.def: Wide from one side to the other.
examples: The book is thick.
The wall is thick.
The ice is thick.

more.def: Having a large distance between two sides, or not flowing easily.
examples: The thick book had five hundred pages.
The soup was thick and hearty.
The ice on the pond was thick enough to skate on.

easy.def: To get thicker.
examples: Flour will thicken the soup.
The fog thickened.
The sauce thickens.

more.def: To become or make something thicker.
examples: Mom added flour to thicken the soup.
The fog began to thicken.
The sauce thickens as it cooks.

easy.def: A thick group of bushes or small trees.
examples: A rabbit hid in the thicket.
The thicket is thick.
We walked through the thicket.

more.def: A dense group of bushes or small trees.
examples: A thicket of brambles blocked the narrow trail.
We pushed through the thicket of thorns.
Deer slept in the thicket.

easy.def: How thick something is.
examples: The thickness of the ice.
Measure the thickness.
The thickness of the book.

more.def: The distance through something from one side to the other.
examples: The thickness of the ice was four inches.
Measure the thickness of the board.
The thickness of the fog hid the road.

easy.def: A person who steals.
examples: The thief ran away.
The thief took the bike.
Police caught the thief.

more.def: A person who steals things.
examples: The thief took a bike from the yard.
The guard chased the thief.
In the story, a sneaky thief stole the king's crown.

easy.def: The upper part of your leg.
examples: I hurt my thigh.
The thigh is above the knee.
My thigh is sore.

more.def: The part of your leg between your hip and your knee.
examples: I pulled a muscle in my thigh.
The thigh is the top part of your leg.
The water came up to her thighs.

easy.def: The bone in your upper leg.
examples: The thighbone is long.
A thighbone is a bone.
I broke my thighbone.

more.def: The long bone in the upper leg, also called the femur.
examples: The thighbone is the longest bone in the body.
The doctor looked at the thighbone.
The skeleton had a long thighbone.

easy.def: A small cap that protects your finger when you sew.
examples: She wore a thimble.
The thimble is small.
A thimble is metal.

more.def: A small cup-shaped cap worn on the finger to protect it while sewing.
examples: Grandma wore a thimble to push the needle through the cloth.
A silver thimble sat in the sewing box.
The thimble protected her finger from the sharp needle.

easy.def: A very small amount.
examples: A thimbleful of water.
She took a thimbleful.
Only a thimbleful.

more.def: A very small amount, as much as a thimble holds.
examples: She poured a thimbleful of milk.
He had only a thimbleful of juice.
A thimbleful of salt was enough.

easy.def: Not thick.
examples: A thin line is on the paper.
The ice is thin.
I read a thin book.

more.def: Not thick or fat, with only a small distance from one side to the other.
examples: A thin layer of ice covered the pond.
The thin book took only a day to read.
She spread a thin coat of butter on the toast.

easy.def: Any object, or something you do not name.
examples: What is that thing?
I packed my things.
The best thing is cake.

more.def: An object, a fact, or an idea that is not named exactly.
examples: There was a strange thing in the box, but I did not know what it was.
The most important thing is to stay safe.
She put all of her things in a bag before the trip.

easy.def: A thing whose name you forget.
examples: Pass me that thingamabob.
What is that thingamabob?
It is a thingamabob.

more.def: A word used for something whose name you cannot remember.
examples: Hand me that thingamabob.
What does this thingamabob do?
He tinkered with a strange thingamabob.

easy.def: A thing whose name you forget.
examples: Hand me the thingamajig.
What is that thingamajig?
It is a thingamajig.

more.def: A word for something when you forget what it is called.
examples: Pass me that thingamajig, please.
What does this thingamajig do?
He fiddled with a funny thingamajig.

easy.def: A word for something when you do not know its name.
examples: Hand me that thingy.
What is that thingy?
I lost the thingy.

more.def: An informal word for something whose name you cannot remember or do not know.
examples: Hand me that thingy on the table.
What is that little thingy for?
I lost the thingy that goes on top of the jar.

easy.def: To use your mind.
examples: I think about my pet.
She thinks hard.
We thought of a good plan.

more.def: To use your mind to form ideas or to have an opinion.
examples: I think it will rain before lunch because the clouds are dark.
He is thinking about what to draw for the art show.
What do you think the answer is?

easy.def: A person who thinks hard and has good ideas.
examples: She is a deep thinker.
The thinker sat quietly.
A clear thinker.

more.def: A person who thinks carefully and deeply about ideas.
examples: She is a deep thinker who asks big questions about the universe.
The class was full of creative thinkers.
The old thinker sat by the fire and pondered.

easy.def: Number three in order.
examples: I am third in line.
She won third place.
Today is the third day of camp.

more.def: Coming after the second and before the fourth.
examples: My brother came in third place in the race.
We live on the third floor.
It was the third time we visited the zoo.

easy.def: As the third thing.
examples: Thirdly, add the milk.
Thirdly, wash up.
Thirdly, say thanks.

more.def: Used to show that something is the third point or step.
examples: First mix the flour, then add the eggs, and thirdly stir in the milk.
Thirdly, check your work.

easy.def: The feeling that you need to drink.
examples: I felt thirst after the race.
The water stopped her thirst.
He drank to stop his thirst.

more.def: The need or wish to drink something.
examples: I felt great thirst after the long run.
A cold drink stopped her thirst on the hot day.
The hikers were suffering from thirst after hours in the sun.

easy.def: Wanting a drink.
examples: I am thirsty.
The dog is thirsty.
We were thirsty after the run.

more.def: Needing or wanting something to drink.
examples: I am thirsty after playing soccer.
The thirsty dog drank from its bowl.
The thirsty plant drooped in the sun.

easy.def: One more than twelve.
examples: I have thirteen stickers.
My cousin is thirteen.
Thirteen birds sat on the wire.

more.def: The number 13, which comes after twelve and before fourteen.
examples: A baker's dozen means thirteen.
She turns thirteen next month.
Thirteen players sat on the bench.

easy.def: Number 13 in a row.
examples: It is my thirteenth birthday.
He was thirteenth in line.
She sat in the thirteenth seat.

more.def: Coming after the twelfth one and before the fourteenth.
examples: My brother will celebrate his thirteenth birthday in May.
She finished in thirteenth place in the race.

easy.def: Number 30 in a row.
examples: It is her thirtieth birthday.
The thirtieth day.
He came thirtieth.

more.def: Coming after the twenty-ninth.
examples: My aunt will celebrate her thirtieth birthday soon.
It was the thirtieth day of the month.
She finished in thirtieth place.

easy.def: The number 30.
examples: I have thirty stickers.
Thirty days are in June.
There are thirty kids in my class.

more.def: The number that comes after twenty-nine, written 30.
examples: There are thirty students in my class.
June has thirty days.
We walked for thirty minutes.

easy.def: A word for a thing that is close to you.
examples: This is my toy.
I like this.
Look at this!

more.def: A word used to point to a person or thing that is near you or that you are just about to talk about.
examples: This is the book I told you about.
Try this juice, because it is made from fresh pears.
These shoes are too small for me now.

easy.def: A prickly plant with purple flowers.
examples: The thistle is prickly.
A thistle grew.
The thistle has purple flowers.

more.def: A plant with prickly leaves and purple flowers.
examples: The thistle scratched my leg.
A thistle grew by the fence.
The thistle is a prickly plant.

easy.def: The middle part of an insect's body.

An insect has a thorax.
The thorax holds the legs.

more.def: The middle section of an insect's body, between the head and the tail, where the legs are attached.
examples: An ant's legs are attached to its thorax.
The thorax of a bee holds its wings and legs.
An insect's body has a head, a thorax and an abdomen.

easy.def: A sharp point on a plant.
examples: The rose has a thorn.
A thorn stuck my hand.
Be careful of the thorns.

more.def: A sharp, pointed part on the stem of some plants, such as roses.
examples: She pricked her finger on a rose thorn.
Blackberry bushes have thorns to protect them.
He carefully pulled a thorn out of his sleeve.

easy.def: Covered with sharp points.
examples: The rose is thorny.
A thorny bush.

more.def: Having thorns, or hard to deal with.
examples: The thorny rosebush scratched my arm.
A thorny branch snagged my sleeve.
The team faced a thorny problem.

easy.def: Complete, with nothing missed.

more.def: Careful and complete, with nothing left out.

The doctor gave her a thorough check for any problems.

easy.def: A fast, fine horse bred for racing.

more.def: A fast, tall horse of a special breed that is raised for racing.

A thoroughbred needs careful training before a race.
The farm raises thoroughbreds that run in races.

easy.def: A main road.

The thoroughfare was wide.

more.def: A main road or public way that people use to travel through a place.
examples: The busy thoroughfare was full of cars.
A wide thoroughfare ran through the middle of town.
The thoroughfare was closed for the parade.

easy.def: In a complete way, with nothing left out.
examples: Wash your hands thoroughly.

more.def: Completely and carefully, leaving nothing out.
examples: He washed his hands thoroughly with soap and warm water.
The detective thoroughly searched the room for clues.

easy.def: A word for things that are not close to you.
examples: Those are my shoes.
Look at those birds.
I like those.

more.def: A word used for more than one person or thing that is farther away or has already been named.
examples: Those mountains in the distance are covered with snow.
Do you remember those cookies we baked last winter?
Those are the books I borrowed from the library.

easy.def: A very old word for "you."
examples: Thou art kind.
In old books, thou means you.
Long ago, people said thou.

more.def: An old-fashioned word for "you" that is found in very old books and poems.
examples: "Thou art welcome here," said the knight in the story.

easy.def: Used to say something that you may not expect.

more.def: In spite of the fact that; although.

easy.def: An idea in your mind.
examples: I had a happy thought.
She shared her thought.
That is a nice thought.

more.def: An idea or opinion that comes into your mind, or the act of thinking.
examples: I had a funny thought while I was watching the clouds.
After some thought, he chose the blue paint.

easy.def: Kind and thinking of others.

The card was thoughtful.
A thoughtful gift.

more.def: Showing that you think about other people's feelings and needs.
examples: She is a thoughtful friend who always remembers birthdays.
The card was a thoughtful surprise.
He gave a thoughtful answer after thinking carefully.

easy.def: In a careful or kind way.

She thoughtfully wrote a note.
He thoughtfully held the door.

more.def: In a way that shows careful thinking, or care for other people.
examples: He nodded thoughtfully before he answered.
She thoughtfully wrote a thank-you note.
He thoughtfully held the door for us.

easy.def: Not thinking of other people.

more.def: Not thinking about how your actions affect other people.
examples: It was thoughtless of me to forget her birthday.

easy.def: The number 1,000.

Count to one thousand.

more.def: The number 1,000, which is ten hundreds.
examples: A thousand meters make one kilometer.
Thousands of fans cheered for the team.
The ancient tree is over a thousand years old.

easy.def: Number 1,000 in a row.
examples: He was the thousandth visitor.
The thousandth day.
The thousandth page.

more.def: Coming after nine hundred ninety-nine others.
examples: He was the thousandth visitor to the museum.
It was the thousandth time she had read the story.
The thousandth car crossed the bridge.

easy.def: A thin string for sewing.

more.def: A very thin strand of cotton or other fiber that is used for sewing.

easy.def: Very old and worn thin.

The sock is threadbare.

more.def: Worn so thin by use that the threads show.

more.def: Something that could cause harm, or a warning that harm may come.

easy.def: To say you might hurt someone.

more.def: To say or show that something bad may happen.

more.def: In a way that seems to warn that something bad may happen.
examples: The dog growled threateningly at the stranger.

The wasp buzzed threateningly near our picnic.

easy.def: The number 3.

more.def: The number 3, which is one more than two.

The farmer counted three eggs in the nest.
We waited three days for the package.

easy.def: Three times as much.

The threefold reason.

more.def: Three times as great or as many; having three parts.
examples: There was a threefold increase in visitors.
The plan was threefold.
The reason was threefold.

easy.def: To beat plants so seeds fall out.

The machine threshes.

more.def: To beat or shake wheat or other crops to separate the grain from the stalks.
examples: The farmer threshed the wheat in the barn.
A machine can thresh a field of grain in a day.
They threshed the oats by hand.

easy.def: A machine that separates grain from plants.
examples: The thresher separates grain.

The farmer used a thresher.

more.def: A machine or person that separates grain from the stalks.
examples: The farmer used a thresher to separate the wheat.

easy.def: The strip of floor at the bottom of a door.

easy.def: Three times.

more.def: Three times; an old way of saying it.

easy.def: Using money carefully.

more.def: Careful use of money and things so as not to waste them.

easy.def: A feeling of great excitement.

more.def: A sudden feeling of great excitement and joy.

easy.def: To make someone very excited.

more.def: To give someone a feeling of great excitement.

easy.def: An exciting story or movie that keeps you on the edge of your seat.

The thriller was exciting.
A mystery thriller.

more.def: A book, a movie or a play with an exciting story full of suspense that keeps you waiting to see what happens.
examples: The thriller was full of twists, and I could not stop reading.

The movie was a thriller about a missing treasure.

easy.def: Very exciting.

The race was thrilling.

more.def: Very exciting and full of action.

easy.def: To grow well and be healthy.

more.def: To grow strong and healthy, or to do very well.
examples: Tomato plants thrive in warm, sunny weather.

easy.def: Growing well and healthy.

The thriving shop was busy.

more.def: Growing, doing well and being successful.
examples: The thriving garden was full of tomatoes.

easy.def: The front of your neck, or the tube inside.

more.def: The tube inside the neck that carries food and air, or the front of the neck.

The doctor looked at my throat.

easy.def: Deep and rough in the voice.

more.def: Deep and rough, as if from the throat.

The engine gave a throaty roar.

easy.def: To beat or ache with a steady pulse.

more.def: To beat or ache with a strong, steady pulse.

easy.def: A steady beat or ache.

A throb in my thumb.

more.def: A strong, steady beat or pulse, or a steady ache.
examples: I felt a throb in my sore thumb.
The throb of the engine shook the boat.
A throb of music filled the air.

easy.def: Beating or aching in a steady way.
examples: My toe is throbbing.
The throbbing music was loud.
A throbbing pain in my thumb.

more.def: Beating or aching with a strong, regular pulse.
examples: My thumb was throbbing after the bump.
The throbbing music shook the floor.

easy.def: A big chair for a king or queen.

more.def: A grand chair where a king or queen sits.

easy.def: A big crowd of people.

easy.def: In one side and out the other.

more.def: From one end, side, or part of something to the other.

easy.def: To send something through the air with your hand.

easy.def: Made to be thrown out after use.
examples: A throwaway cup.

more.def: Made to be thrown out after use.
examples: We used throwaway plates at the picnic.

easy.def: A person who throws.

easy.def: A small brown bird with a spotted chest that sings.

easy.def: To push something hard and fast.

easy.def: A dull sound of something heavy falling.

more.def: To hit something with a dull, heavy sound.

easy.def: A dull sound, like something heavy falling.

more.def: A dull, heavy sound made when something falls or hits a surface.

more.def: To hit or fall with a dull, heavy sound.

more.def: A sudden, loud crash of thunder.

easy.def: Very shocked.
